title: Sections of a limit with epimorphic transitions
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $(F_n)_{n\geq1}$ an inverse system of abelian sheaves on
$X_{\Proet}$ with epimorphic transition maps, and $F=\varprojlim_nF_n$. Then the
canonical map $F\to R\varprojlim_nF_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\Proet})$, and
for every object $W$ of $X_{\Proet}$

$$
R\Gamma(W,F)\simeq R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)
$$

in $D(\mathbf Z)$; here $R\varprojlim$ of a sequence $(K_n)$ is the fibre of
$1-\text{shift}\colon\prod_nK_n\to\prod_nK_n$.

proof.text:
The topos $X_{\Proet}$ is replete ([sk-prop-pe-replete]). In a replete topos, for
an inverse system of abelian sheaves with surjective transition maps,
$R^1\varprojlim F_n=0$ and the higher derived limits vanish, i.e.
$R\varprojlim_nF_n\simeq\varprojlim_nF_n$ (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 3.1.10);
equivalently the map $1-\text{shift}\colon\prod_nF_n\to\prod_nF_n$ is an
epimorphism with kernel $F$, and countable products of sheaves are exact on a
replete topos so that $\prod_nF_n$ computes the derived product.

The functor $R\Gamma(W,-)\colon D(X_{\Proet})\to D(\mathbf Z)$ is triangulated and,
as a right adjoint, preserves products. Applying it to the triangle
$R\varprojlim_nF_n\to\prod_nF_n\xrightarrow{1-\text{shift}}\prod_nF_n\to$ gives the
triangle defining $R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(W,F_n)$, whence the isomorphism.
